summary: Gregory Schopen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Black Hills State, McMaster, Washington, and ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, he held professorships at Indiana, UT Austin, and UCLA.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich. He held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Moscow State University.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.

Gu Jiegang worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Taiyan Zhang and Shih Hu, later holding posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Guang Xing is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett, and held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from ~1984 to 2006, and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2006.
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Bonn, Münster, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner and Michael Hahn), held research posts in India and Japan, and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She completed her Doktorgrad der Philosophie and PhD at the University of Munich, studying under doctoral supervisor Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Gudō Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who studied law at the University of Tokyo and under Kodo Sawaki and Renpō Niwa. He founded Dogen Sangha International and lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991 and 2008).

Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of London and SOAS, later serving at University College, Colombo and as Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from around 1986 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from ~1926 to 1933 and subsequently held a post there from ~1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, and served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen alongside several other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Kent, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught English at Baring Union Christian College, religion at Columbia, and held a Sikh Studies chair at UC Santa Barbara.

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1893–1901) and later held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, later serving there as a Senior Teaching Fellow (attested 2014).
